chapters.title: Chapter 3: TDS on Investment Income and Other Payments

lessons.title: TDS on FD and Recurring Deposit Interest: Thresholds for Regular and Senior Citizens

body.text: The 10% your bank deducts from FD interest is a placeholder, not your tax. Your real tax on that interest is your slab rate, which could be zero or could be 30%. TDS tells you nothing about which.

children.text: Lata, 58, is a school principal in Nagpur who keeps her savings in fixed deposits. In tax year 2026-27 she earns ₹1,12,000 of interest across three institutions. Only two of them deduct TDS, and the total deducted is just ₹7,000. She is in the 20% slab of the old regime, so her actual tax on that interest is far higher. By the end of this lesson you will know exactly why each institution behaved the way it did, and what Lata still owes.

markDefs.definition: The amount of interest a single payer can pay you in a tax year before it must start deducting TDS. Once crossed, TDS applies to the entire interest, not just the excess.

children.text: TDS on interest from deposits sits in Section 393(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, Table, Sl. No. 5(ii) and 5(iii) (formerly Section 194A). The rate is a flat 10% for residents who have furnished a PAN. What changes is the

children.text: Three details decide whether TDS kicks in, and most people get at least one wrong.

cells: Per bank, not per branch or per deposit
All your FDs and RDs across every branch of the same bank are added together, because banks run on a single core banking system
Per tax year, on interest credited or paid
Interest the bank credits or accrues between 1 April and 31 March counts, whether or not the FD has matured
Cross the threshold by ₹1 and TDS applies to the whole year's interest from that bank. ₹50,001 of interest means ₹5,000 of TDS, not 10 paise

body.caption: Why only two of Lata's three institutions deducted TDS

cells: State Bank of India (2 FDs and an RD, different branches)

children.text: SBI added up both FDs and the RD across branches and still stayed below the bank threshold. HDFC Bank crossed it, so the entire interest was taxed at source. Bajaj Finance is a non-banking company, so the far lower threshold applied.

body.title: Quick Check: Does Splitting Deposits Help?
body.question: Karthik, 45, expects ₹90,000 of FD interest from one bank. He is thinking of moving half his deposits to another bank so each pays ₹45,000. What happens?
options: He avoids TDS and also avoids tax on the interest
He avoids TDS, but the full interest is still taxable at his slab rate
Nothing changes, because the threshold counts interest across all banks
He avoids TDS only if he also opens the deposits in different branches
body.explanation: The threshold applies per bank, so ₹45,000 from each bank stays below ₹50,000 and neither deducts TDS. But TDS is not the tax. The whole ₹90,000 is still his income, and both banks report it to the department, where it shows up in his AIS. Splitting only postpones the payment to filing time.

body.text: Every rupee of deposit interest is reported to the Income Tax Department whether TDS is deducted or not. It appears in your Annual Information Statement. Leaving out interest that had no TDS is one of the most common reasons salaried people and retirees receive mismatch notices.

children.text: Cumulative FDs: TDS Before You See a Rupee

Many depositors believe a cumulative or reinvestment FD escapes TDS until maturity. It does not. Banks credit or accrue interest every year, and TDS is due on whichever comes first, credit or payment. Take Farida, 42, in Lucknow, who puts ₹8,00,000 in a five-year cumulative FD with Punjab National Bank at 7.25% compounded quarterly.

body.caption: Interest accrued and TDS each year on a ₹8,00,000 cumulative FD

body.title: Farida's yearly accrued interest vs the ₹50,000 threshold

children.text: The FD grows to about ₹11,45,809 and she receives nothing until maturity, yet the bank deducts TDS every single year because each year's accrued interest crosses ₹50,000. The table assumes the bank recovers TDS from her linked savings account. Some banks deduct it from the FD itself, which slightly reduces the compounding. Either way, she should report the accrued interest as income each year to match what the bank reports.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Company FD Limit
body.textWithBlank: A company or NBFC deducts TDS on FD interest once the interest it pays you in a tax year exceeds ₹___.
body.explanation: Bank and co-operative bank deposits get the higher ₹50,000 (or ₹1,00,000) limit. Company FDs, NBFC deposits and most other interest payers use the ₹10,000 limit, which is why a modest company FD often has TDS when a larger bank FD does not.

children.text: The bank deducts the same 10% whether you earn ₹3,00,000 a year or ₹30,00,000. Interest is added to your other income and taxed at your slab rate. So for some people 10% is too much and for others it is far too little. Here is ₹1,00,000 of FD interest from one bank for someone below 60, at different marginal slab rates, including 4% cess.

body.title: Tax on ₹1,00,000 of FD interest vs TDS deducted

children.text: Now back to Lata. In the 20% slab, her tax on ₹1,12,000 of interest is ₹1,12,000 × 20% × 1.04 = ₹23,296. Her three institutions deducted only ₹7,000 between them, so she still owes ₹16,296 on this interest when she files, or earlier as advance tax.

body.title: Try It: The 30% Slab Depositor
body.prompt: Vivek, a senior manager in Gurugram, is in the 30% slab. He earns ₹2,40,000 of FD interest from ICICI Bank this tax year, and the bank deducts 10% TDS. Including 4% cess, how much more tax does he owe on this interest beyond the TDS?
body.explanation: Actual tax is ₹2,40,000 × 30% × 1.04 = ₹74,880. TDS was ₹24,000. He owes ₹50,880 more. Since that is well above ₹10,000, he should pay it as advance tax during the year, or tell his employer through Form 122 so it can be recovered through salary TDS, to avoid interest under Sections 424 and 425.

body.title: Scenario: Mr Raghavan Turns 77
body.scenario: Mr Raghavan, 77, a retired railway officer in Chennai, receives a pension of ₹4,80,000 a year and earns ₹2,20,000 of FD interest, both through Canara Bank. He has no other income. Last year the bank deducted ₹22,000 of TDS on his interest, and his son had to file a return to claim a refund.
body.prompt: How can he avoid both the TDS and the return this year? Assume he uses the new regime and Canara Bank is a specified bank.
body.modelAnswer: Because he is over 75, resident, and his only income is pension and interest from the same specified bank, he qualifies as a specified senior citizen. He should give Canara Bank Form 125 (formerly Form 12BBA). The bank then computes his total income and tax itself, instead of deducting a flat 10% on interest. His taxable income is ₹4,80,000 of pension less the ₹75,000 standard deduction, plus ₹2,20,000 of interest, which is ₹6,25,000. That is within the ₹12,00,000 rebate limit, so his tax is nil and the bank deducts nothing. Having furnished the declaration and had tax computed by the bank, he is not required to file a return. Without Form 125, the bank would again deduct ₹22,000 under the normal interest rules, and a return would be needed to recover it.

body.title: Joint FDs: whose PAN gets the TDS?

children.text: Banks deduct TDS and report the interest against the PAN of the first holder on a joint deposit. The threshold is also tested against that first holder. That can be misleading. For tax, interest belongs to the person whose money funded the deposit, and income from money gifted by one spouse to another is generally taxed back in the hands of the spouse who gave it.

If a retired father is the first holder on an FD funded entirely by his daughter, the TDS credit sits in his AIS while the income is really hers. Keep the first holder aligned with whose money it is, or be ready to explain the difference in both returns.

body.title: Audit This Year's Interest and TDS
steps: List every FD and RD you hold, grouped by bank or company, with the expected interest for tax year 2026-27
Add up interest per bank and compare with the ₹50,000 or ₹1,00,000 threshold, and ₹10,000 for company FDs
Include accrued interest on cumulative FDs, not just interest paid out
Estimate your actual tax on the interest at your marginal slab and compare with 10% TDS
If the gap is large, plan advance tax or declare the interest to your employer through Form 122
Open your AIS and confirm every bank's interest figure, including those that deducted no TDS

body.label: Annual Information Statement (AIS)
body.description: Log in to the e-filing portal and open AIS to see interest reported by every bank, post office and company, alongside any TDS deducted.

points: Banks deduct 10% TDS on deposit interest above ₹50,000 a year (₹1,00,000 for senior citizens), and companies above ₹10,000, under Section 393(1), formerly 194A
The threshold is counted per bank across all branches and deposits, per tax year, and once crossed TDS applies to the entire interest
Cumulative FDs suffer TDS every year on accrued interest, even though you receive nothing until maturity
TDS is a flat 10%, but interest is taxed at your slab rate, so taxpayers in higher slabs owe more at filing and those with nil tax get refunds
Splitting deposits across banks can avoid TDS but never avoids tax, because all interest is reported in your AIS
Seniors get a higher threshold, can use Form 121 if their tax is nil, and at 75 or above can use Form 125 with a specified bank to skip filing a return
